title: Terraform user agent validation and isolation on URL Filtering rules

prose.text: Up to v4.8.8 the provider validated URL Filtering user agents against a shorter list than some of its sources. {{validator-omits-brave}} {{validator-shared-by-three-resources}}

prose.label: BRAVE.
prose.text: {{header-profile-accepts-brave}} {{hcl-cannot-declare-brave}} {{issue-606-report}} The contract and the provider disagreed on SSL Inspection up to v4.8.8 and disagree on Cloud App Control from v4.8.9 {{divergence:brave-provider-vs-contract}}. {{read-copies-user-agents}} Whether a read can fail on a BRAVE value is not established {{gap:issue-606-read-time-failure}}.

checks.do: Whether a rejected `user_agent_types` value is BRAVE, which the provider validator omits for three rule resources.
Whether the tenant has Cloud Browser Isolation before configuring an `ISOLATE` rule, and whether the rule has a `cbi_profile`, no OTHER user agent type and only HTTP and HTTPS protocols.

validator-omits-brave.statement: Before v4.8.9 the provider's `user_agent_types` validator accepted OPERA, FIREFOX, MSIE, MSEDGE, CHROME, SAFARI, MSCHREDGE and OTHER, and omitted BRAVE. v4.8.9 adds BRAVE to the list (#607).
validator-omits-brave.conditions: Changed upstream in v4.8.9 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "In v4.8.8 the provider's `user_agent_types` validator accepts OPERA, FIREFOX, MSIE, MSEDGE, CHROME, SAFARI, MSCHREDGE and OTHER, and omits BRAVE."

validator-shared-by-three-resources.statement: The shared `getUserAgentTypes()` schema applies that validator, and `zia_url_filtering_rules`, `zia_ssl_inspection_rules` and `zia_cloud_app_control_rule` all use it for `user_agent_types`.

header-profile-accepts-brave.statement: Up to v4.8.12 the `user_agent` criterion of `zia_http_header_profile` was validated against a list that includes BRAVE. v4.8.13 makes `user_agent` a free custom user agent string, for use when `user_agent_bitmap` is OTHER, and the list (still including BRAVE) validates `user_agent_bitmap` (#613).
header-profile-accepts-brave.conditions: Changed upstream in v4.8.13 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "The `user_agent` criterion of `zia_http_header_profile` is validated against a list that does include BRAVE." That `user_agent` has no validator at v4.8.13 rests on reading its schema entry, which has Type, Optional and Description only.

evidence.after: Description: "The user agent evaluated by the criteria.",

quotes: "user_agent": { Type: schema.TypeString, Optional: true, Description: "A custom user agent string to match. Use it when user_agent_bitmap is set to OTHER.", },
Description: "The user agent bitmap evaluated by the criteria.", ValidateFunc: validation.StringInSlice([]string{
[PR #613](https://github.com/zscaler/terraform-provider-zia/pull/613) - `zia_http_header_profile`: `user_agent` in `http_header_profile_criteria` accepted only the predefined browser values
It now accepts any string, for use with `user_agent_bitmap = "OTHER"`.

hcl-cannot-declare-brave.statement: Before v4.8.9 HCL could not declare BRAVE in `user_agent_types` for URL Filtering, SSL Inspection or Cloud App Control rules, although the HTTP header profile accepted it; from v4.8.9 all three accept it.
hcl-cannot-declare-brave.conditions: Follows from the validator list and the three resources sharing it. Changed upstream in v4.8.9 (checked 2026-10-18): previously "So under v4.8.8 HCL cannot declare BRAVE in `user_agent_types` for URL Filtering, SSL Inspection or Cloud App Control rules, although the HTTP header profile accepts it."

read-copies-user-agents.statement: The URL filtering Read copies the API's `UserAgentTypes` into state.

isolate-needs-cbi.statement: Creating a URL Filtering rule with the `ISOLATE` action requires the Cloud Browser Isolation subscription.

quotes: Creating a URL Filtering rule with the action of `ISOLATE` requires the Cloud Browser Isolation subscription.
This block is required when the attribute `action` is set to `ISOLATE`

isolate-validation.statement: For an ISOLATE rule the provider requires a cbi_profile, rejects the user agent type OTHER, and allows only HTTP and HTTPS protocols.

quotes: cbi_profile attribute is required when action is ISOLATE
user_agent_types should not contain 'OTHER' when action is ISOLATE.
when action is ISOLATE, valid options for protocols are: HTTP and/or HTTPS

issue-606-report.statement: Provider issue #606 reported that the ZIA API returned BRAVE in `user_agent_types` for existing rules and that `terraform plan` then failed with the validator error on a list of eight values ending in OTHER; a repository member closed it as completed on 2026-10-01 saying v4.8.9 resolved it.

quotes: The ZIA API already returns it for existing rules
## Comment (MEMBER, 2026-10-01) @(user) Issue has been resolved in the latest version v4.8.9. Please upgrade.
`terraform plan` fails with a validation error when the ZIA API returns `BRAVE` as part

brave-provider-vs-contract.summary: Whether BRAVE is an accepted user agent type on SSL Inspection and Cloud App Control rules.

positions.says: The captured Automate contract includes BRAVE in the SSL Inspection `userAgentTypes` enum.
The contract omits BRAVE from the Cloud App Control `userAgentTypes` enum.

expect.description: User Agent types on which this rule will be applied

positions.says: The provider validator used by both resources omits BRAVE.
From v4.8.9 the provider validator used by all three resources includes BRAVE.

brave-provider-vs-contract.impact: Under v4.8.8 an SSL Inspection rule that the API allows to carry BRAVE could not be written in HCL. From v4.8.9 the provider accepts BRAVE on SSL Inspection, agreeing with the contract, and also on Cloud App Control, where the contract omits it; whether the API accepts BRAVE there is not established.

issue-606-read-time-failure.title: Whether the API returns BRAVE for existing URL Filtering rules and the provider then fails planning
issue-606-read-time-failure.blocks: saying that a URL Filtering plan fails on read for rules with broad browser selections
issue-606-read-time-failure.detail: Issue 606 (issue-606-report) reports that the API returned BRAVE for existing URL Filtering rules with broad browser selections and that the provider failed during plan. The Read path copies the API value into state and the sources here do not show a validation failure mechanism on read. Reproduce in a scratch tenant with a URL Filtering rule that selects all browsers, then plan with v4.8.8. v4.8.9 adds BRAVE to the validator (validator-omits-brave). The fixing commit's message (e8b12a9, not a citable file) says the backend now returns BRAVE for URL Filtering rules and that the validator then failed with `got BRAVE`; whether that failure happened on read, as the issue reports, is not shown.
